howDoI.q: How do I warn the player before something happens?
How do I make something happen again and again?
How do I make something hurt only once?
How do I make several things take turns?
How do I make a floor that vanishes and comes back?
How do I let the player fall without losing a life?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Warning First is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels and nothing in it can cost a life.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score.

Things here warn you before they do anything: a vent rumbles before it puffs, and a plank flickers before it vanishes. Watch for the warning, then go.

pages.head: Level 1: Rumble, Then Puff
pages.html:
Level 1: Rumble, Then Puff

Three fog vents sit in the ground. Each one rests, then rumbles for about two seconds (the grate hops, little gold shake marks appear and a few bubbles rise), then puffs a column of gray fog for about a second and a half, then rests again. A puff stings a little: it takes 10 hit points, once.

The first sign says the ground rumbles first. The second says to wait for the puff to end, then go. Stand on the first vent and see what happens, and you will find out what the signs mean. After that, wait for each puff to end and cross at once: there are about five seconds of rest, and crossing takes two.

The vents take turns, because each one rests a different time the first time round. There are four coins on the way, worth ten points each.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • A vent is a ring of blocks. Open one.bbl in the blocks editor and pick v0.a.rumble. Its Next block is v0.a.puff and its Time is 40 ticks. v0.a.puff lasts 30 and turns into v0.a.rest, which lasts 90 and turns back into v0.a.rumble. Because the last block points back to the first, the vent goes round for ever. There are 18.2 ticks in a second.
  • Three cells a vent. A vent is the grate in the ground (v0.g, solid, so Rima can walk over it), and two blocks of fog over it (v0.a, v0.b). Each cell has its own ring with the same times, so they change on the same tick and look like one thing.
  • The warning is a block. The rumble block is the same as the rest block with shake marks and wisps drawn on it. It is also a different shape from the puff, so a player who cannot tell the colors apart can still tell a rumble from a rest.
  • Taking turns. The block on the map is v0.a.start, a rest that looks like the others but lasts 90 ticks the first time, v1.a.start lasts 140 and v2.a.start 190. After that all three rings are the same length and stay that far apart.
  • Stinging once. The lower fog block while puffing, v0.a.puff, takes 10 hit points and has a Touched block: v0.h.start. A touched block changes the map cell for good, so after the first sting that cell belongs to a twin ring, v0.h, with the same times, the same pictures and no sting. If it took hit points every time it was touched, Rima would lose them every tick she stood in it. Each vent stings once.
  • The clock starts with the level. Every timer is set when the scene loads, which is why a level card comes first.
  • The walls. A hedge closes the room in at both ends.

pages.head: Level 2: Flicker, Then Gone
pages.html:
Level 2: Flicker, Then Gone

Two bridges of planks cross a pit, with a grassy island between them. A bridge is solid for about six seconds. Then it flickers for two seconds (gold and black stripes, and it is still solid) and then it is gone for three, and then it is back.

The first sign says a flicker means gone, so get off. Stay on the planks and you will fall two blocks onto a soft mat. Nothing is lost: hop out and wait for the bridge to come back, then cross while it is solid. The second sign says the planks come back.

The two bridges are out of step, so one is often solid while the other is not. There are four coins: two on the island, two on the far bank.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • A plank is a ring of three blocks. Open two.bbl. p0.solid is solid and lasts 108 ticks, then turns into p0.flicker. That is also solid, but striped, and lasts 36. Then it turns into p0.gone, which has no Solid box and shows the pit, and lasts 54. p0.gone turns back into p0.solid.
  • Still solid while it flickers. The warning is not a danger: the flicker plank holds you up, so you have two seconds to step off. A warning that already dropped you would not be a warning.
  • The two bridges. p0.start lasts 108 ticks the first time and p1.start lasts 54, so the second bridge is half a cycle ahead.
  • The pit. Under each bridge is a column of pit block (a deep blue backdrop that the hero falls through, because it pulls down) and, at the bottom, a solid mat with a gold cushion on it. Falling two blocks costs nothing. Game-Maker has no fall damage.
  • Climbing out. The pit is two blocks deep, and a jump is higher than that, so there is no ladder.
  • The walls. A hedge closes the room in at both ends, and the pit's sides are dirt you can see.

pages.head: What Game-Maker cannot do
pages.html:
What Game-Maker cannot do

A warning in Game-Maker is only a block that changes first. Some things you may expect are not there:

  • It cannot start a warning when the player does something. Every timer starts when the scene loads, so a vent cannot rumble because Rima got close, and a plank cannot start to flicker when she steps on it. The warning is something to watch for, not something she sets off.
  • It cannot tell a block where the player is. A vent does not know whether Rima is near, so it puffs whether anyone is there or not.
  • It cannot wait for the player. The rumble lasts as long as you wrote and then the puff comes, ready or not.
  • It cannot play a sound when a block changes. The warning has to be something you can see.
  • A block does not know what its neighbors are doing. Each cell of a vent has its own ring, and they agree only because their times agree.
  • It cannot hurt only once with a plain timer. A hurt happens every time Rima touches the block, so the sting needs the touched-block trick on the page about level 1.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • In one.bbl, change v0.a.rumble's Time from 40 to 80 to give the first vent a longer warning. Change v0.b.rumble and v0.g.rumble too, or the cells will drift apart.
  • Make the rest block shorter, and the vent puffs more often.
  • Change v1.a.start's Time and the second vent puffs at another moment.
  • In two.bbl, shorten p0.flicker's Time to make a harder warning, or lengthen it to make an easier one.
  • Draw your own flicker picture for a plank, in the blocks editor.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
